sprint_goal: Clear the full ready frontend-correctness, design-consistency, and security-hardening slate across all 25 scoped stories

ST-01.title: Fix GET /analytics/tag-performance 500 on staging (missing trade_tags column ensure)
ST-01.notes: Root cause: get_tag_performance_endpoint() never called ensure_trade_plans_table() before querying trade_tags, unlike every trade_plans.py route. Fixed by adding the ensure call (narrow endpoint-level fix, RISK-03 either candidate acceptable). No spec deviation - implementation now matches documented contract; the bug was a runtime defect, not a spec gap. Verified via tests/test_trade_plan_tags.py (14 passed) and trade_plan-scoped regression run (46 passed). docs/ops/api_performance_baseline.md updated to record resolution.

ST-02.title: Confirm api-key-cross-environment-check.yml is genuinely running, not silently skipping
ST-02.notes: Reclassified delegated_backend -> autonomous at execution time (planning-time assumption was that this needed live external dashboard/production access; in practice `gh api repos/.../actions/jobs/<id>/logs` on the already-authenticated gh CLI was sufficient -- no Render/Supabase dashboard or new credential needed). AC-1: confirmed via the 2026-08-09 scheduled run's real log (run 31299858987) that the check genuinely executes with real secrets, not silently skipping -- STAGING_API_KEY was added 2026-08-08 (confirmed via `gh secret list`). AC-2: found and hardened a different, more serious gap live in that same log -- a PROD_API_URL read timeout crashed the script with an unhandled exception, and the workflow's alert step could not distinguish that from a genuine cross-wired-keys finding (both were non-zero exit code), producing a false-positive 'keys cross-wired' Telegram alert. Hardening decision (recorded per AC): fail loud not silent for both failure classes, but keep them distinguishable -- probe() now returns None on network error (never conflated with a real finding via evaluate_environment's new ok=None outcome); missing-secrets skip-guard now emits ::error:: and exit_code=2 instead of silently exiting 0; workflow has two separate alert steps (exit_code 1 = cross-wired security finding, exit_code 2 = probe/config error, inconclusive). Verified via tests/test_api_key_cross_environment.py (8 passed, 4 new). No spec deviation -- api_key_security_register.md entry #6 updated to record the live-confirmation and the hardening in the same commit.

ST-06.title: Register muted/muted-foreground (and other dead -muted classes) in tailwind.config.js
ST-06.notes: Registered `muted`/`muted-foreground` in tailwind.config.js theme.extend.colors (Design Pre-Approved). Verified via a real `tailwindcss` CLI build -- all 5 in-scope -muted classes (bg-muted, border-muted, fill-muted, fill-muted-foreground, text-muted-foreground) now compile to non-empty rules with real hsl(var(--muted...)) declarations (previously empty). Playwright coverage added: SC-CP-13/SC-CP-14 in command-palette.spec.js. Could not execute Playwright locally in this sandbox (Chromium install unsupported on this OS) -- real GitHub Actions CI (playwright.yml, runs on pull_request) is the verification path per LL-v8.3-P3-02. No spec deviation -- Case D (CI/tooling config change with no prior canonical spec; tailwind.config.js is the de facto spec reference). Discovered and filed BLG-FE-147/BLG-FE-148 (out-of-scope findings) for the broader sibling tailwind-token gap and remaining untested call-site families. CRITICAL FINDING (real CI, first run): SC-CP-13/14 failed with the light-theme value instead of dark -- root cause traced to src/Layout.js: the literal 'dark' CSS class (required by darkMode:['class']) was only ever applied to Layout's own wrapper div, never to document.documentElement, so Radix's DialogPortal (renders into document.body, outside that wrapper's subtree) has always put every Dialog-based component app-wide (14+ consumers) in light-theme CSS scope regardless of the user's actual theme -- a pre-existing, systemic production bug this story's new tests were simply the first to observe. Fixed at the root: Layout.js now also syncs the dark class onto document.documentElement (an ancestor of every portal). See qa_evidence_EPIC-03.md for full writeup.

ST-07.title: Frontend wiring to populate trade_plans.thesis_model_version/thesis_prompt_version on save
ST-07.notes: Root cause: backend already fully supported thesis_model_version/thesis_prompt_version (Create/Update models, database.py INSERT/UPDATE whitelist) but the frontend form state (src/pages/TradePlan.js) never captured them -- the real Claude response from POST /trade-plans/generate-plan (the 'Improve with AI' button) includes model_version/prompt_version but the success handler only destructured d.fields, discarding them. Fixed: (1) 'Improve with AI' handler now sets form.thesis_model_version/thesis_prompt_version from the real response; (2) new setNarrativeField() helper clears both fields on any manual edit to setup_thesis/entry_rationale/confirmation_criteria/early_exit_conditions (replacing the ad hoc setup_thesis-only isAiDraft/isClaudeDraft reset and the plain set() calls for the other 3 fields); (3) the client-side-template 'Generate thesis' button (not real AI -- generateThesisTemplate() is a deterministic string builder) also clears both fields, since it was never Claude output; (4) existing-plan load now carries the persisted values forward so re-saving an unedited AI plan doesn't lose them. No backend change needed -- fields were already in the Create/Update Pydantic models and the update whitelist. Playwright coverage: SC-TP-24a/b/c in tests/e2e/trade-plan.spec.js (save-payload interception pattern, extending the existing SC-TP-23f precedent) -- AI path populates both fields, template path leaves both null, edit-after-AI clears both. Could not execute Playwright locally in this sandbox (Chromium unsupported on this OS); real CI (playwright.yml) is the verification path per LL-v8.3-P3-02. No spec deviation.

ST-09.title: Design token audit: v6.7 contrast fix consistency
ST-09.notes: Audit-only completion (RISK-02, per sprint_backlog.md Notes) -- no code fix made in-story. Branched from EPIC-03 tip (not main) per RISK-01: auditing against main's pre-ST-06 CSS baseline would have been auditing a known-broken baseline (main doesn't yet have ST-06's tailwind.config.js muted-token fix merged). Method: grep-based scan of src/**/*.js for drift against the v6.7 canonical secondary-text token (text-slate-600 dark:text-slate-400), filtering out icon-component usages (out of scope per the v6.7 decision record's own §5 scope boundary). Found 6 real drift instances across 2 sub-classes: 4 use the failing light-theme shade text-slate-500 instead of text-slate-600 (Positions.js, PositionCard.js, WatchlistRow.js, Layout.js's search button+kbd badge -- the kbd badge's dark value is also wrong, both branches use the pre-v6.7 failing shade); 2 are missing a dark: variant entirely (Reports.js reconciliation note, WhatsNewCard.js bullet+overflow item). No dark:text-slate-500 misuse found anywhere. Filed BLG-FE-149 (consolidated, P3) per this story's AC. Full findings: st09_secondary_text_token_audit_findings.md.

ST-10.title: Empty-state illustration/microcopy consistency pass
ST-10.notes: Design Required, decision already resolved at Design Gate; design_system.md v1.8 already documented the pattern pre-implementation (AC-1 pre-satisfied, confirmed). Implementation: fixed TradePlans.js's trailing-period heading ('No trade plans yet.' -> 'No trade plans yet') per the decision record's own named fix. Scanned all emptyHeading= call sites app-wide (18 found, beyond the 4 the decision record audited) and found one additional undisclosed deviation with the identical bug: CalendarView.js ('No closed trades yet.' -> 'No closed trades yet') -- fixed in the same commit per the decision record's own instruction to align any additional deviating call sites found during implementation. Updated the one stale Playwright selector this broke (saved-filters-calendar-view.spec.js SC-SFC-09). ST-11.title: Confirm theme-toggle persistence across sessions
ST-11.spec_reference_not_applicable_reason: audit + correctness fix, no prior canonical spec governs the theme-persistence mechanism itself (design_system.md only passingly mentions a header theme toggle) and no new artefact created that would serve as one
ST-11.notes: Audit traced the full mechanism (src/Layout.js): localStorage.getItem('theme') || 'dark', a literal 'dark' CSS class applied to the root wrapper div (required by tailwind.config.js's darkMode: ['class'] for every dark: variant app-wide to activate at all -- verified this is the only such mechanism in the codebase). Persistence itself was already correct for both AC scenarios: a long-gap fresh session (localStorage has no expiry) and a storage-clearing event (clean fallback to 'dark' default, no error). Real gap found: theme state defaulted to 'dark' in useState and only self-corrected in a post-mount useEffect, so a persisted 'light' theme flashed dark on every load/reload before correcting. Fixed (not filed, per this story's Notes allowing either): lazy-initialise useState directly from localStorage instead of defaulting+correcting, removing the flash entirely. Added data-testid/aria-label to the two theme-toggle buttons (previously icon-only, no accessible name -- needed to make SC-TP-04 testable). Playwright coverage: tests/e2e/theme-persistence.spec.js SC-TP-01..04 (light/dark persisted-value-applies-immediately, no-persisted-value fallback, toggle-then-reload persistence). Could not run Playwright locally in this sandbox (Chromium unsupported on this OS); real CI (playwright.yml) is the verification path.

ST-12.title: Mobile responsive audit for PerformanceAnalytics page
ST-12.notes: Design Pre-Approved (corrective-only against already-approved analytics.md v2.0 layout spec). Audited page + all 18 analytics sub-components against analytics.md's documented Responsive Behavior section. Found and fixed 4 real drift instances: (1) TimeBasedCharts.js Day-of-Week grid was fixed grid-cols-5 with no mobile breakpoint (~69px/cell at 375px width) -> grid-cols-3 sm:grid-cols-5; (2) MonthlyHeatmap.js drill-down modal table missing overflow-x-auto (spec requires horizontal scroll on all tables; 4 sibling table components already had it) -> added; (3) RMultipleAnalysis.js R-Multiple-by-Tag table had the same missing-overflow-x-auto gap -> fixed; (4) PerformanceAnalytics.js's period-selector+export-button header row was a bare flex row with no stacking, contradicting the spec's own 'stack or compress at smaller widths' claim -> flex-col sm:flex-row, matching PageHeader's own convention (both empty-state and main-content header instances fixed). Confirmed correct, no change needed: ExecutiveSummaryCards/MarketComparison/TopPerformers/BestWorstTrades grids already match spec exactly; 4 other table components already had overflow-x-auto; RMultipleAnalysis's grid-cols-2 stats grid is fine at mobile width (no fix needed). Playwright coverage: tests/e2e/analytics-mobile-responsive.spec.js SC-PA-M01..06 (mobile-viewport assertions for all 4 fixes, plus 2 desktop-regression checks confirming unchanged behaviour at lg width). Could not run Playwright locally in this sandbox (Chromium unsupported); real CI (playwright.yml) is the verification path.

ST-13.title: Dark/light theme contrast audit follow-up
ST-13.notes: Audit-only completion (RISK-02). Cross-checked ST-09's secondary-text token audit (same EPIC) via a different sampling method (component-level review, not class-string grep) -- confirmed no additional secondary-text drift beyond ST-09's 6 instances (BLG-FE-149). Real new finding, connected to this EPIC's ST-06 dark-mode-portal fix: checked 5 real Dialog-based components' DialogContent styling -- 4 hardcode bg-slate-900/text-white unconditionally (always dark regardless of app theme setting; not a WCAG contrast failure since it's internally high-contrast, but a light-theme completeness gap); the 5th (CommandDialog) correctly relies on the shared theme-aware tokens, which is exactly why it was the one place ST-06's portal bug was actually observable. Filed BLG-FE-150 (design-scope question for Head of UX & Design: is dark-only modal styling intentional?) -- not fixed in-story since it requires a design decision, not a mechanical correction. No further contrast gaps found.
